statement: When more than one observation exists for a race, the current-best row is chosen by source tier first (official state election authority outranks media aggregator), then by completeness of reporting units, then by recency. A later timestamp alone never promotes a record.
why: A newer aggregator capture must not displace an older official count. Recency is the weakest of the three signals.

statement: A race enters headline and margin figures only when it carries a complete count from the state election authority and no source integrity flag. Three races qualify: Texas, Virginia, Wyoming.
why: Prevents a partial or unverified count being quoted as a result.

statement: A source carrying an unexplained integrity marker is excluded from headline figures regardless of how complete its count is. Montana is flagged for a TEST marker.
why: Completeness says nothing about whether the source is a production system.

rule: Leader votes and race total are distinct
statement: leading_votes is one candidate's votes. race_total_votes is every candidate added together. They are never alternative figures for the same quantity and must be labelled so on every visual.
why: A reviewer compared the two columns across versions and read them as conflicting snapshots. The arithmetic reconciles exactly in all six official states.

rule: Exploratory visuals carry n and a no-causation label
statement: The money-against-outcome scatter is labelled exploratory, states its n, encodes count quality by transparency, and carries no trend line or correlation statistic.
why: Finance data stops 14 October; the election was 3 November. Association only, and the comparable cohort is 108 of 619 filers.

statement: Any observation about who raised most is stated as a property of the selected reporting cohort, never as a general partisan pattern.
why: 511 of 619 filers report on other periods or none, and are not in view.

statement: Checks are never silently dropped between versions. Every check carries an origin_check and a lineage value: Retained, Restored, Consolidated into, Superseded by, or Resolved and retired.
why: 12 checks were dropped from v2 to v3 without a record. All are restored and re-run in v3.1, giving 51 checks.

rule: Dated snapshot, not a live tracker
statement: Every page carries the collection date. The report is presented as a dated research snapshot and makes no claim to track results as they change.
why: Counts will keep moving and states will certify later.
